en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
7. The Mansion of Pesavatī “I beheld a most delightful mansion, covered with lattices of crystal, silver,
and gold, and with a floor of various colors.”
This beautiful celestial mansion is well-constructed,
adorned with archways, and strewn with radiant gems;
it shines through the ten directions like the sun in the sky.
Just as the autumn moon, the dispeller of darkness with its thousand rays,
shines upon this celestial mansion of yours,
so does it blaze like a crest of smoke over the night sky.
Like a lotus flower with eyes of shimmering radiance,
this beautiful form is fixed as if in space;
it resounds with the music of lutes, drums, and cymbals.
Prosperous as the city of Indra is this place of yours.
There are lotuses, water-lilies, blue lilies, and white esculent lilies,
as well as *yodhika*, *bandhuka*, and *nojaka* flowers.
The *aśoka* trees are covered with blossoming *sāla* flowers;
this place is frequented by the sweet fragrance of various trees and shrubs,
entwined with *saḷala*, *labuja*, and *bhujaka* vines.
A delightful, glorious lotus pond, resembling a lattice of jewels, has appeared for you, with flowering kusa-grass creepers hanging down over it.
Whatever species of flowers grow in water,
and whatever species of trees grow on land—
whether they belong to humans, non-humans, or the divine.
All of you were born in your dwelling.
What is the ripening of this self-restraint and self-control?
By what fruit of karma have you been reborn here?
"And just as this celestial mansion was attained by you, so too did I attain it; speak of that, O Śilārapamha.
"And just as this celestial mansion was attained by me..."
It was frequented by flocks of peacocks, pheasants, and cakora birds;
it was graced by divine swans and royal cranes,
and resounded with the songs of parrots, kāraṇḍava ducks, and cuckoos.
Adorned with various *santānaka* flowering trees and diverse species of *pāṭali*, *jambu*, and *asoka* trees—
just as this celestial mansion has been attained by me.
I shall declare this to you; listen, venerable sir.
To the east of the excellent city of Magadha, there is a village named Nāḷaka, venerable sir.
There, in the past, I was a daughter-in-law;
there they knew me as Pesavatī. I [served] him who was skilled in the meaning and the Dhamma, having honored him.
To the great Upatissa, immeasurable and extinguished, who is honored by gods and men,
I joyfully scattered flowers.
And having worshipped the Supreme One who has reached the ultimate goal,
the sublime Seer bearing his final body,
[he] abandoned this human aggregation.
“I shall not dwell here; I am going to the realm of the Three [Goddesses].
Thus ends the seventh vimāna, Pesavatī.
